content.text:
I submitted **index 2 (Fe 0.84 / Sb 0.16)**, which had the highest EQE of the three samples I measured: **0.177%**.

All 3 merit measurements are used. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Fe / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.88 / 0.12 | 0.131 |
| 2 | 0.84 / 0.16 | **0.177** |
| 13 | 0.51 / 0.49 (FeSbO4) | 0.005 |

- **Model predictions:** MACE put hematite (Fe2O3) and FeSbO4 on or very near the stability limit. MEGNet predicted band gaps of about 2.77 eV for hematite and 2.08 eV for FeSbO4, so both should absorb at the 2.7 eV light.
- **What I measured:** Even so, the FeSbO4 composition performed about 25 times worse than the Fe-rich end. That points to Sb-doped hematite as the working material. Going from 12% to 16% Sb raised EQE further.
- **Remaining uncertainty:** The best composition could still be somewhere between about 20% and 45% Sb, which I didn't measure. The model-based suggestion tool ranked 20–24% Sb (indices 3–4) highest for the next measurement. I also left the Sb-rich end untested, because EQE dropped so sharply on the way to the 1:1 composition.
